# Cloak

> Cloak is a privacy-first PDF redaction tool that runs entirely in the browser. It uses on-device AI to detect and redact personally identifiable information (PII) from PDF documents. No file is ever uploaded to a server — all processing happens locally on the user's device.

## What it does

Cloak lets users drop a PDF, automatically detects PII using a named entity recognition (NER) model running in the browser via WebGPU or WASM, and produces a redacted PDF with black boxes over sensitive content. The redacted file can be downloaded immediately.

PII types detected include: names, email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses, organizations, and other named entities depending on the model in use.

## How it works

1. User drops or selects a PDF on the landing page
2. The NER model (loaded via @huggingface/transformers, running on-device) extracts text from the PDF page by page using PDF.js
3. Detected entities are shown to the user for review
4. User confirms redactions; mupdf applies permanent black-box redaction annotations to the PDF
5. The redacted PDF is available for download

All processing is client-side. No network requests are made with document content.

## Key facts

- URL: https://cloakdoc.app
- Free to use, no account required
- Works offline once the page and model are loaded
- Supports any text-based PDF (not scanned image PDFs)
- Built with React, Vite, PDF.js, mupdf, and @huggingface/transformers
- Model runs via WebGPU when available, falls back to WASM on CPU

## Pages

- [Home / Upload](https://cloakdoc.app/): Drop a PDF to begin redaction
